After hundreds of hours invested in this game I can say it's fun, but there are enough flaws to drive away the majority of players. The development of this game stalled after about two years, leaving a playable but unsatisfying experience overall. There are several zones to explore in this game, each offering many different types of missions and rewards. The final zone is a half finished area only accessible by players who have reached the level cap.
Over the years content has been added, including pvp and pve content, allowing players to enjoy hundreds of hours of entertainment. Some of the fixes and additions frustrated some of the more experieenced players and made it nearly impossible for new players to realy enjoy anything beyond the first parts of the game.
Leveling is slow going without help from experienced players. With the right help it's possible to reach the level cap in two days or less. Reaching the skill point cap is a different matter. Plyers will need to dedicate at least a hundred hours to optional races that award points that will improve their character's "build". It's important to choose the right build and figure out how to exploit the various skill sets. WIth the right skill set players are able to dominate pvp matches and earn death toll. These pvp points can be spent on power-ups and gear that can't be purhcased or crafted. Some of the pvp gear can be purchased through the auction house for a considerable sum.
Making money is pretty easy with the right recipes. Selling items such as ammo and fuel at the auction house makes it possible to eran money farely quickly, but the best money comes from selling serendipity items and boss loot. Although the best gear and weapons come from earning death toll, the next best thing is crafted with rare and unique items found in the later zones.
I definitely recommend this game for someone looking for a open-world rpg. Although the game is free to play it isn't pay to win. Premium membership does have it's perks though. WIth a minimal premium purchase players can reach the level cap in a few hours, but most premium items are purely cosmetic. Respec injectors are overpriced, so I recommend using guides to make an ideal build from the start. RPG players that enjoy fps games will have may ours of enjoyment even if the graphics are pretty dated.

I dont usually feel urge need to write review for games..but when i do..
Earth 2150, in one sentence:  "The Forever Shining jewel of the past".
This game not only stands for itself, but it stands for an era of gaming and gaming industry.
Its the era when studios care to impress the gaming population and offer as much content as possible and with quality to come with, and wasn't driven by money as first priority.
This is not your typical C&C game that after 7 missions of singeplayer sends u back to your desktop to spend $$$ for expansions packs, or the studio was "too lazy" to add naval units or other core features.
Earth 2150 came out in 2002, and set a new era of RTS gaming, since it was (if im not mistaken) the first full 3D RTS game in the market.
-The Story in a nutshell:
its 2150, and the over-use of nukes in the recent wars by 2 of major factions has resulted in kicking the earth out of its normal orbit straight into the sun.
So now the earth's destruction is inevitable and led to all 3 factions working on big projects to evacuate (their) popluation to Mars before the earth explodes.
-Gameplay
This is not your typical Paper-Rock-Sccisors RTS/ this unit counters that and that counters this .....
You research tech, which comes in the form of Chasis for ur vehiciles/ships/aircraft.
You also research a large variety of weapons, and ammunitions, togather you build those weapons on top of ur units creating different type of units according to your taste, different chasis sometimes allow u to combine weapons togather.
The maps are big, and the approach to attack is different in each game, especially vs other players, since its hard to forsee what tech he is going for; is my enemy rushing rockets tech with homing capabilites? or hes going right into plasma cannons or air units?
You can manipulate the terrain , create trenches to block enemy vehicles, flatten the terrain, build bridges, and...construct an entire tunnel network...yup...u can literally dig under fortified enemy bases for back-door attacks.
Most weapons require ammuntions, so u need to consider this when fighting far from your base (supply depots and aircraft handle ammunition delievery).
Campaign-
The Beauty of the campaign is that its no entirely linear; you are set with a global objective of getting a large amount of credits towards the evacuation of the planet.
Within missions u need to find the balance between building an army and researcing tech, to sending credits to ur spaceport for the main goal, if u fail missions the game doesnt end, sometimes u just lose the tech/content that u could have received withing that missions, and in some cases u are presented with different missions on the globe due to the one u failed.
you only fail the campaign if u fail to achieve the required credits when the timer runs out ( and you have plenty of time, the timer doesn't pushes you to rush missions at all), i finished the first campaign with 109 days left (out of 183) and i took all the time in the world in each and every mission i played.
The missions vary from destroying enemy bases, sneaking and exploring huge tunnel systems, recovering artifacts and prototypes, testing new tech and the usuall destroy your enemies.
You can finish the campaign earlier, u dont need to reach "final mission 20" to end the game, its all up to your methods.
you do u have general time limit before earth goes boom though..
When the global timer gets close to zero, the map variety changes as well, forests map turn into lava maps with hot terrain,
water maps are almost non existent...and so on.
Its also worth to note that during the campaign, the enemy faction also research their weapons, just like you, the AI doesn't have advantage over the player, and excluding a few techs, the AI research advancement depends on your playstyle.
Turtling usually lets the AI finish all hes availabe research and keep up with the player, sometimes bypass you.
Playing aggressively, and attacking research centers or finishing missions early, sets the AI back, not allowing it to finish its research, creating an advantage for the player in future missions.
in total, there are around ~30 missions..yes....THIRTEE missions PER faction , and they usually take more then 30-40 min real time to complete.
Just to give an exmaple, it took me around ~20 total hours to complete the campaign with one faction.
Its insane how much content and variety this game has for something that comes up in 2002, most of those features the RTS games of today doesn't even have, and the content they provide is much more thinner.
You are always driven forward to continue, if its by the tech and the new units that come available, the missions, the story and so on.
I wish studios today would develop games like earth 2150, and its concepts that completly change the course of how RTS games work. rather then squeeze as much $$$ as possible for its costumers and giving them the minimum content to please them.
Its amazing that im enjoying this game even more when i first played it..12 years ago.
For a miserable price of 7 bucks which includes the expansion packs as well, its so much worth it.
Im playing this game on Win 7 with no problems at all, if its crashes for u its due to resultion, and there are plenty of solutions to that in steamforums/internet.
TL:DR
Pros:
-Non-linear campaign
-Very long campaign
-Multiple ways to approach missions
-Unit Costumization and a very large research tree
-Air force, Navy Units and Ground Units, its all there
-Tunnel digging
-Minefields
-Terran shaping and manipluation
-Very intresting to play factions, all balanced and differ from each other
-Hige Replay value
Cons
-Old controls and lacking mouse options (you canno't invert the mouse controls - right click command, left click select)
-Sometimes clunky units behevior (units shooting rockets into mountains etc..)
-Not alot of players in mutiplayer these days
Overall 9.5/10

Absolutely one of the BEST RTS games out there. I've bought this game three times already... In any case, the gameplay is just as innovative now as it was back in... Well, I don't remember. I was literally a kid then. Games are only just now starting to pick up on the complexity and customization that this game brought to the table, and its graphics honestly still look pretty damn good, especially considering its age.
On the note of graphics, on both my hard copy and
copy, there is widescreen incompatibilities that will crash the game. This is simply because widescreen didn't actually exist when the VooDoo APIs (remember those beasts?) were written. Fixing it is fairly simple though. Look up nGlide, download the driver package and executable, configure and enjoy. Basically what it does is trick that old VooDoo software into thinking it is still in 4:3 while you're running 16:9 or 16:10 formats, plus it'll work with any game that was programed for those old VooDoo GPUs. Mechwarrior 3, here I come!
Gameplay wise, this game is both forgiving and unforgiving. The campaigns are long, and its amongst the few games that allows you to continue the campaign even after losing missions and battles. That's the forgiving part... The unforgiving part is that the game is basically a resource rush, battling relentless and challenging AIs over resources and trying to mine them out and send them back to your main base. While the game gives you plenty of opportunity to achieve your goals, the AI is very intelligent, and will stop at nothing to end you. Failing and/or fumbling battles too much will result in watching your people die in a firey apocalypse, and there won't be jack♥♥♥♥♥♥you can do about it. That being said, there is a huge number of missions for each campaign, some of which are only available under certain circumstances such as "Lose here..." or "Win there..." or the like.
The game provides a huge variety and complexity in units, weapons, and research, all of which makes for customizable units to a degree unseen in RTS with the exception of maybe Sid Meier's Alpha Centauri. Throughout the game, whether in single or multiplay, you're have to balance cost, quality, quantity, and power for your units, weapons, and research, and rushing tech is much more complex than you'd see in other RTS like StarCraft or Dawn of War. Overall, each faction has a huge variety of units and lacks the over-simplified "this unit counters this" dynamic that seems to be so prevalent in RTS these days.
If this game has shortcoming at all, and obviously I don't think it does, it would be in its story. The game runs on a simple premise, described in the manual, box, and on the Steam page, of "The world was nuked to death by UCS Robots, and its orbit was disrupted enough that it's orbit has started to destabalize and move ever closer to the sun... So GTFO of dodge." Granted, a little bit more story is conveyed through mission briefings which are simple emails that you can read, but they can be generally skipped and are rather dull outside of the odd running joke. You make your own story in where you choose to go in the capaigns, and how you choose to handle each battle. Personally, I prefer this method, as games like Homeworld 2 get obnoxious with their incessant in-game cutscenes and endless hand-holding. I'd rather play my game, not watch it.
Overall, I'd say that Earth 2150 is the most innovative RTS out there, and certainly amongst my favorites along with Dawn of War, Homeworld, and the first StarCraft. It surpassed its predecessor "Earth 2140," and set a high bar that its sequel, "Earth 2160," sadly fell just short of. If you're a hardcore RTS player, I highly recommend this game.
I forgot to mention a couple things... The controls are quite unfamiliar. Being amongst the first 3D RTS games out there, they messed with the controls quite a bit. Being that this game lacks a tutorial, I strongly suggest downloading the manual, or finding a quick reference guide for the controls. Also, the prerendered cutscenes in this game are pretty damn awesome. Sadly, they are compressed to hell because they use the old bink codecs, but the quality really is top notch. Think about what CG looked like in 2000, then compare it to this... Really, the only places you'll find better is in studios like Blizzard.

One of the first games I remember buying as a kid was 18 Wheels of Steel: Convoy.  I remember enjoying it profusely.  10 years later, American Truck Simulator provides the same enjoyment.  Beatiful scenery, great graphics, and realistic trucks and trailers all combine to make an enjoyable experience for those who remember playing hours of 18 Wheels of Steel games many years ago.  However, no review of ATS is complete without mentioning the slightly dissapointing lack of content. I noticed a lot of bad reviews, so I'm here to talk a bit about the game itself.
I understand why people are unhappy with the game, it has been in development for a
time it seems as if there's not a lot of progress being made. That seems true, and it's a valid criticism.
That said, I don't believe that is enough of a reason to not recommend the game. The physics and the combat engine are phenomenal, and it's genuinely fun to play. It's a challenge sometimes and I feel that there's a bit of learning curve before you begin to feel competent when you're fighting against AI (admittedly I don't play many fighting games). The attention to detail is amazing to me. The animations, the way you sheath or "holster" your weapons, the way you hold them, the movement, the stealth take downs, jumping/climbing for the most part, dodging and flipping, dragging enemies and picking up or dropping objects... it all just feels so fluid. Very fluid. Impressively fluid. Hell, after slitting an enemy's throat, the way that their blood squirts, spills, pools, and drips onto surfaces in itself is morbidly captivating. But the way this is executed (pun intended) really goes to prove that detail and polish are both a very important part of making a good game. Which I honestly believe this is.
The Lugaru campaign (port) is definitely fun, but it's also lacking. I will admit that if the game's own campaign is as lacking in terms of story, cutscene, dialogue, or enviornment or "tasks"/missions I will be upset. There's no multiplayer yet, and the arena mode again is really fun but somewhat lacking.
Again, I understand that it needs a lot of work. That does not make it bad, or not fun to play. If the game is released in full and not updated much, or is deficient in terms of content I wouldn't hesitate to negate this review and actually not recommend the game. Developers should, in a way, be held accountable.
So reader, this is what I suggest: buy this game on sale if you're interested. I hope you like it as much as I do and appreciate the work that has been put into it. Let's hope the final release and following patches are even better!

I made a guide to the keyboard shortcuts for this program in the Community Hub.
A light version of Howler.... has essentials, but compared to Howler, has very little.  Compared to most digital painting software, it has a truckload of tools.  'run as administrator' mode may be required.  All tool grouping and keyboard shortcuts are non-standard and will make sense after a while.
My 4 year old loves to use this program as of recent to paint.  My wife also enjoys using this program to paint.  It's a lot more than people think it is.  It's too bad people aren't playing with it more to see that
Update: While the content in buffers appears to not save while in buffers, I've found that the Swap buffer will save when using the lyr save option.  The brush buffer(store brush) saves out and imports separately.
Update: As of more recent testing, I'd say DCI 2K Native(2048 x 1080) is as large as you should go if you're planning to use the various plugins(k), like starfield.
Update: As of most recent testing, PD Particles seems to handle A4 720ppi on my computer. (It does not handle A4 1200ppi on my computer.)  To put this into numbers, normal HD is 1280 x 720, nice HD is 1920 x 1080, yet A4 720ppi is 5953 x 8419.
There are no negatives at this price.
In what ways is Particles unequal to Howler?
Particles lacks a great many filters which Howler has and the depth of many filters that are available when compared to Howler's version of those filters.  Animation Cells(animation cells inside of custom brushes are in Particles) and Video Editing are not present in Particles, but are present in Howler.  Creating mountains and clouds through generated 3d extrusion/beveling and effects in Howler using the 3d designer is not present in Particles.  3d extrusion for graphs, walls, and roughed out cities is in Howler through Puppy Ray, but is not in Particles.  It seems to me that Howler 10 has more processor available to it for functions, perhaps it is better at utilizing the GPU when it needs to or perhaps it is better at utilizing the CPU more fully when it needs to.  There are more menu options for the various buffers in Howler 10, you can simply do more with various buffers in Howler 10 than in Particles 9 because the menu options are there to select.
In what ways is Particles equal to Howler?
The brushes.  Particles has the particles, bristles, orbicles, foliage brush types, and the fx buffer brush styles, the animated custom brushes, and the detailed customization of the brushes.  Saving custom brushes as images so the transparency works in the png file format is present too.  If you focus on painting and appreciate the unique benefits that digital brushes can offer, then Particles is as good as Howler in many ways.  If you live in the highway lane of digital shortcuts, then Particles isn't a good fit for you.
In what ways is Particles unequal to natural painting?
If you're used to the brush... digital is... never perfect, but it has it's advantages that are worth experiencing.
However, if you do chinese/japanese painting with multi color loading, direction and pressure and rotation determining your gradients on the fly, use speed to create effects of hardness, and do everything in one stroke watching the watercolor lighten slightly each stroke till gone, and only loading the tip when desired to keep a thin dark for a leaf or part of a flower petal ...then there is nothing out there that does this.  Maybe someday, but for now, the emulation just doesn't exist.  The speed emulation exists on Fresh Paint by Microsoft and there are other attempts to create this... but if you do this style of painting, don't expect a digital equivalent, because there isn't one available.

Five hours in, and I can't get enough of this game.
If you like isometric hack and slash rpgs, and a decent challenge, this is the game for you. The gameplay's tight, and requires a certain level of skill so that you don't get wrecked, even on normal. The visuals are decent for the type of game it is, and for when it came out, but aren't going to win any awards. The main strengths of this game come in the boss fights, which are varied and unique, and will destroy you the first few attempts. The level design is also standout, and makes exploring for equipment and items more interesting.
The story's pretty weak, and really just serves to move your character from area to area, but the dialogue is cheesy enough to make up for it. And the music, while mostly being decent, never really does anything spectacular, and can, though rarely, be grating.
All in all, for the first game in a long running series to try something new, it really comes together as more than the sum of it's parts, and what it lacks in polish, it makes up for in charm.

This game is absolutely phenomenal !
Not because of a story, which is barebone and extremely cliche, but for the action and gameplay. Ys is of course from a long line of older ARPG, but if you would like to compare it to a modern game, that would be Super Meat Boy or Dark Souls. All 3 of theses games share the same philosophy. They are tough as nails, but they are fair.
Ys is all about skill. You discover new enemies, new bosses, and at the beginning it seems completely impossible, all the odds are stacked against you. Then you start noticing the attack patterns of the enemies. Then you start countering them and damaging them. Then you start feeling in control. But suddenly, with the boss at mid health, it is now using new patterns, and killing you fast ! But then you start noticing patterns again...and the circle can continue again...
You will die in Ys. You will die a lot in Ys. You will despair, you will rage against the game. But in your heart, you know the game is fair, it is just asking you to hone your skills to prove worthy of victory. And when finally, after countless retries you will manage to defeat that boss you've been stuck on forver, all your previous despair will turn into pure joy, and a feeling of true accomplishment.
All of that will also be amplified by the beauty of this game. Even though it's obviously dated, the rich environements and superb boss attacks will make you wonder how modern games can look so boring. Ys: The Oath in Felghana reminds me of Secret of Mana or The Soul Blazer series. It's a hack and slash rpg where you slay monsters and kill tough bosses to progress through the entire game. I liked Oath in Felghana because after playing Ys Chronicles, the game remains true to the series even if you can't bump into enemies anymore. So what did I think about it? Lets see...
Graphics: This game is a port from the PSP version that was released a few years ago. I liked how Oath of Felghana now has 3d backgrounds or monsters but still maintains a 2d layout. The sprites look nice if you set your graphics to the highest, but I personally think they are simple. I still find the game to great, even with it's cutscenes which look decent but could be better.
Sound: I really thought the sound department went forth and had fun making the music. There are good songs, but I just don't find myself to play over and over again. Sound effects are pretty basic, but I don't think that matters. There was never a moment where I just wanted to put my own music to the game which is a plus in my own opinion.
Gameplay: If you played Ys Chronicles, you realize that you can't bump into enemies like you used to for exp. There's now an attack button which can be used to string combos to gain exp. What I find the most rewarding is the three magics you obtain in the game. My favorite is probably the wind power since you use it to get to treasures and to another section of the level. If there is one thing I really enjoyed the most are the bosses. Playing on past normal is a challenge as it requires you to be quick about your actions and for you to time your attacks. The game is hard if you're not leveled correctly but it doesn't take you long to be strong enough to take on a boss.
Overall: I consider Ys: The Oath in Felghana a great purchase if you enjoy J-rpgs that aren't complex, yet easy to play but difficult to master. I think falcom did great with this remake because it adds a new chapter in the Ys storyline for American audiences and it is faithful to the first two Ys games in the series.

It's also the most polished and bug-free of the STALKER games. Despite its shortcomings Call of Pripyat is recommendable simply because it works. It has a lot of content in both items and quests, it's very free-roam right from the start and it's overall the most accessible of the three games.
The storyline is both gripping and enthralling. With many twists and turns throughout, this game will bring out the emotion in even the most cold-blooded of us.

Stock game is a bit lacking in vehicle roster, but this should improve soon enough.
ETS2 is the better buy if you don't have it already, having more overall variety and more interesting and immersive drives due to cab articulation and the greater variety in configurations (4x2 trucks with heavy loads are especially interesting/fun at high speed down curved inclines..). That said, American Truck Sim offers a distinct flavor of its own with its American machines and subtly playful maps. I can't wait for future expansions to the northwest and south, and central regions!

One of the first games I remember buying as a kid was 18 Wheels of Steel: Convoy.  I remember enjoying it profusely.  10 years later, American Truck Simulator provides the same enjoyment.  Beatiful scenery, great graphics, and realistic trucks and trailers all combine to make an enjoyable experience for those who remember playing hours of 18 Wheels of Steel games many years ago.  However, no review of ATS is complete without mentioning the slightly dissapointing lack of content.  There are only four playable trucks and there are only three states in the game as of now, making for a much smaller playing area than Euro Truck Simulator 2.  (However, New Mexico is coming soon!)  But ATS is an excellent platform for modding, and there are no lack of mods to keep the game from becoming boring!  In conclusion, this game offers realistic gameplay, great graphics, and a large playing area, but only has four playable trucks and a small map, but this is somewhat midigated by a large number of mods.

I've seen it getting bad reviews recently so i thought i'd add my opinion.
Yes, this game has been in development for a long time and still isn't done. Is that bad? Depends how you think about it. I see it as, the devs are STILL working towards making this game better (and have hired more staff recently so progress is speeding up).
It still doesn't have a campaign (But it has Lugaru which is the previous "game" but a remastered version). The campaign will probably be the last addition before/at release so that's expected. It's better to get the gameplay sorted first.
The game recently got Steam Workshop mod support, which is bringing more user created maps, weapons and other things. It had mods for a while but through steam is much simpler.
SHOULD YOU BUY THIS GAME?
In my opinion, definitely. I've never really been a fan of fighting games but this one does stand out. Instead of having a health bar, you have a much more realistic way to fight. You can get punched in the face once, fall and smash your head on a rock and your neck will snap, killing you instantly. You could fight for minutes getting beaten by enemies, sliced, stabbed and end up looking awful. You never know how a fight will end, and that's what's so great.
This game is about reflexes. Anyone can win any fight, if you know how.
It's hard to explain how satisfying this game is to play, it's probably worth watching some youtube videos of fights to see.
I can understand why some people downvoted this game, but to me it's the perfect fighting game. I've owned it many years and although i don't play it every day, it's always fun to have a quick game, play VS with someone on the same screen, play some mods or just jump into the arena and beat the life out of some poor rabbits.

A deeply immersive game where placing your dynasty on the different thrones of Europe, Western Asia, and North Africa is the main goal. You accumulate score based on the number of empires, kingdoms, duchies, counties, and baronies controlled by your dynasty. The base game allows for nearly 400 years of gameplay in the base version, with close to 300 more years added in DLC.
The base game starts in the year 1066, around the time of the historic Battle of Stamford Bridge. You can start playing during any month and year between 1066 and 1337, choosing any historic ruler you like. You can choose to play as any christian ruler all the way down to the county level, (you can unlock all other religions and cultures with DLC) and you work your way up the ranks. Your ruler's traits determine how much your vassals like you, how much land you can hold, how effective he is as a military leader, diplomatic relations, etc. Marry daughters or sisters of kings for alliances, and have children to ensure the success of your dynasty. You will want to groom your heir as well as you can, but beware of assassinations and other freak accidents.
My only complaint is the amount of the game that's cut out and made into DLC, but when they add DLCs they also add a large amount of free content to base game users, so its not that bad.

I have very mixed feelings on this game, so I guess I will just give a list of pros and cons:
PROS
- GREAT atmosphere. The "breathing" effect that the lights have truly create a sense of panic and dread. The sound is great, going from total eerie silence to droning, wooshy, "something's wrong" queues.
- Very scary. Monkeys are terrifying to begin with to me personally, so to have a 6 foot tall one with red eyes jumping out of nowhere is an♥♥♥♥♥♥clencher for certain.
- Visuals (lighting, smoke, etc.) are nice.
CONS
- Some textures are seriously buggy, and it takes away from the immersion.
- That Tocatta and Fugue in the main menu totally doesn't fit rest of the game whatsoever, and I'd suggest something a little more subtle.
- While hand-holding is never good, an objective being made clear would be cool.
- I experienced a major bug 2 or 3 times where after flashbanging the enemy, my character would be stuck in place, causing me to lose from loss of oxygen. I don't know if there's something I could have done that's not apparent to me, but it seems like something is off there, and it's a total game breaker.
In short, it's a great idea for a game, and the atmosphere and premise are right. All it needs is a little tweaking here and there and it could be great! Right now, it's a little broken, which is understandable of a brand new release.

The game plays like a first person bullet hell, the sound design is amazing and all the creepy scuttling and vworping you hear around you isn't just there to freak you out, but to aurally position enemy hellspawn. The graphical style evokes classic 90's era shooters, and it works extremely well here. Gameplay is stripped down to the absolute bare minimum, there's only one goal; seemingly to stay alive for as long as possible. I think I would've enjoyed the game so much more if there was more to it, some levels to traverse instead of just a straight up endless wave survival mode, but for a game that's whole focus is being so ultra stripped down, it's hard to really fault the pure simplicity of it. And for the price? Not bad at all.

Definitely unique within the current roster of MOBA games. The character cast is smaller than League of Legends or DotA 2, but there's just enough of them to fulfill most roles you'd come to expect — and a few you wouldn't — with more added regularly. Graphics are nice, but can run on lower-end systems fairly well. Music tends to be pretty jammin', too. If you have a poor Internet connection, you might encounter a lot of lag and random disconnections, the former of which can really annoy people since it gives some characters an undue advantage (looking at you, Coco), and a lot of people exploit that intentionally. Still, the community is leagues above most other MOBAs, with people that will actually try to help new players as opposed to bash them as useless scum on the sea floor deserving of prompt immolation, which is a refreshing change of pace. On top of all that, you don't have to pay to unlock characters, as they come the more you play — only extra skins for those characters cost anything, and there's a couple you can get for free, even.
All in all, definitely a fantastic game to pick up. Incredibly fun, gives a taste unlike other MOBAs and a lot of games in general, and is continuing to grow.

I have just sneaked into the Waste Processing Station, which is being used by mercenaries as their camp. I have to find a notebook containing their plans and then return to Owl with the intel.
I am heavily outnumbered and outgunned. If I pick a fight with anyone, I'm dead. If I get spotted, I'm dead before I can get out the door, let alone the compound. Where is the notebook? Somewhere upstairs, I'm sure.
It's so dark I can't see anything immediately around me but the handrail of the staircase silhouetted against the fading daylight from outside. I can't risk using my flashlight. Hugging the deep shadow against the wall, I crouch and move silently. There's the notebook! Got it! Now to get out.
Can I sneak out the same way I sneaked in? I can. I pick up a jerry can of fuel as a bonus on the way out. Not a shot fired (and just as well because ammo is expensive). Who says stealth is dead? Not me! I stop to eat before starting back, just in case I need some energy to sprint for safety.
I almost make it back to the Shadovsk when I'm ambushed by a pack of mutants charging from behind. Just Flesh, so easy to handle. Mission accomplished. I'll head back to  the WPS later when I'm better armed and can hold my own against the mercs: right now I need the money that intel will get me.
No hand holding. No follow the NPC leader. No warnings of any kind of impending death. Just me and the Zone.
I had heard the S.TA.L.K.E.R. series was solid (and was already a Metro 2033 fan) so I bought Call of Pripyat on sale but then it sat there in my Steam library, neglected while I played other newer games. And then I heard about the Misery Mod. It sounded hard. It sounded scary. It looked fantastic. Misery 2.1 is cruelty ratcheted up several notches to the level of sadomasochism.
Run out of medkits? You die. Miss your headshot and don't duck back into cover fast enough? You die. Forget to pop an antiradiation pill? You watch your health slowly bleed out (and then you get into a firefight). It is just the most awesome, scary, thrilling and realistic gaming experience I've ever had.
If you want to experience a game that is as brutal as if you were in the irradiated zone around Chernobyl in real life, Misery Mod 2.1.1 is it.
UPDATE: Heading out from base, whether in Zaton, Jupiter or Pripyat, equipped and loaded for a day in the Zone of Alienation (I have now been freeplaying Misery as a Recon for hundreds of hours) not knowing whether I'm going to encounter mercs or bandits, bloodsuckers or chimeras, wondering if I'm going to locate a new stash (170 looted so far) or just find a new ledge I can climb onto, or even acquire an unknown 23rd artifact type to add to my collection: every day in the Zone is a joy, an adrenaline rush, and a meditation on the beauty of the maps and excellent gameplay that the developers and modders created.
If I were shipwrecked on a desert island (with my PC and a power source) this would be the game I would want with me.

I have been playing STALKER CoP with the MISERY mod, and it is almost everything I could ask for in a game as an adult PC gamer. I have not played vanilla CoP, so this is more of a MISERY review, but from what I have read CoP has managed to deal with many of the shortfalls of STALKER Shadows of Chernobyl. I first purchased SoC based on its strong evaluation for 20 dollars, and was quickly dissapointed. Not so with CoP. The open world made of three large regions is a welcome change to the linear maps of SoC, and the way the anomalies are done is also much cooler and more interesting. With MISERY, it's kind of a more serious, more difficult alternative to Fallout 3. The gun fights are excellent. The mutants are horrifying (especially the blood suckers), and I always feel a great sense of relief when I make it back alive at the end of the day.
CoP with MISERY mod has some very negative reviews from players who have really had a hard time with it. Actually however, I have found it very well balanced and carefully done. It is not "pointlessly" hard, only it may appear to be so if somebody attempts to apply regular FPS logic to its world instead of more of a simulator logic. Those people familiar with games like Operation Flashpoint of the ARMA series shouldn't have too much trouble, once they have figured out how inventory works, and how to deal with radiation, etc. I have only played CoP MISERY for a relatively short time, but in many years of gaming I already rate it as one of my all time favorites. Strongly recommended.

Hello here my review for Divinity Original Sin 2
The game is a downgrade from the first one in all terms.
Most attributes dont mean jack anymore. Wits for example. In the first game your initiative was bases upon it. Who acts first in battle. With high wits your entire team could act before the enemy. Here with high wits and luck one of your character can act first, then a round robin system takes over. You act, one enemy act, you act and so on. Wits = useless stat now.
The power progression is incredible bland. You get 2 attributepoints and 1 skill point per level. A point in strenght gives you 5% more damage for str based weapons. So 10 points in str give you 50% more damage. A point in constitution gives you a little more hp. Int is for spells and int based weapons. Finesse is for ranged and finesse based weapons. Str increases carry capacity. Memory increases spell slots. That is it. Evasion is not governed by your attributes, initiative is useless, you have no mana points, there is no attribute to get more action points. That is just so annoyingly streamlined and simple it makes me angry.
The combat is way too difficult on normal difficulty. You have to upgrade your equip every level to have a chance in the battles. There are way too few battles to get xp in the beginning. Without cheesing and min maxing to the extreme you do not have any chance in one battle. You come to the starter island and have like 3 battles to begin. First you fight against some cockroaches, easy battle. Then you fight against 3 crocodiles that can 2 shot your party members. And you have no tools to overcome this. Even on explorer mode the battles are unfun and too hard. You are a level below the enemies no chance.
The combat system is non-tactical. There is an idiotic armor system working that sucks the fun out of every fight. As long as the enemy has physical or magical armor you can not use a control spell on them. So you have to pick at their armor before you can do use control spells. That takes any kind of tactic out of the fight. You just hammer the enemies and it is good. The control spells when working are too short. It is way better to just outright kill enemies with your hardest damage spells.
Every skill has a cooldown. Yo so fun. You have the healing school water magic. The enemies dish out a lot of damage, so you have to heal your party. But your only healing spell in water magic has a 4 turn cooldown. So you can not heal your party up. What is that kind of stupid design.
So you play a pyrokinetc mage, but your main damage skills have all cooldowns on them. After shooting your damage spells like fireball and fire daggers, you can not do nothing but waving with your want at the enemies for low damage until your spells are ready again, 5 turns or 4. What are doing MMO like cooldowns in a supposedly oldschool roleplaying game?
Enemies get much more action points then your party. They dish out a ton of damage you can only dream of in the beginning and midgame. Later it gets worse and worse. The enemies get tons of armor and hp, dish out more and more damage.
Skills are not explained, all mechanics in the game are not explained at all. You have to find everything out yourself through try and error.
It seems like every mechanic in the game is just made to annoy the player. The battles are stupid. You can not hold aggro, they have zero tactical elements thanks to the armor system and the only difficulty tool the developers use is HP bloat and damage output of the enemies. The enemies magically know that healspells work on your undead character. But you are hiding the fact that you are undead carefully. Is that immersion?
The story is your standart you are the chosen one stereotype go save the world run of the mill fantasy garbage. The highly praised roleplay system with warrior, barbarian or scholar tags context in dialoges is more annoying then anything. Without the right roleplay tags you can not interact with npcs and have no clue what would be working. You miss a ton of content without a guide. For some people this would encourage to replay with another character. But for me the combat is so frustratingly difficult i will just not play the game at all. Roleplaying means that you decide how your character behaves and acts. Here the tags decide how you can react to npcs. That is not roleplaying anymore. It takes away player freedom, which can not be a good thing in my eyes.
The skill system is just bad.
Itemization is very bad. You find an epic item, wow cool for you. But in one or two levels it will just become obsolete because of the power creep of items here in this game. It is a diablo like itemization without the tons of loot opportunities through combat. That is just screwed up. Items in Shops reset every level. Wow so much immersion. So you nearly have to upgrade your equip every level on each of your characters to stay inline with the insane power creep of the monsters. Just insane. And equip costs a ton of money too.
Without knowing and abusing every powerfull skill and every tool you can use in the game you will just have no fun in this game. Even the explorer mode is too difficult. Monsters a level or two above your paygrade? You will loose, tactics do not matter.
Okay you could read guides to know what is good and lower the frustration a lot by playing cockie cutter builds, but where is the fun in that. Do i have to replay the first 3 starter island fight until a find a combination of skills and classes that have a remote chance of getting through the game. It seems to me the game was only made for expert fanatic fans, not the normal player.
I am really annoyed and frustrated by this game and will just stop playing. It is not worth playing for me.
The enivroment, music and atmossphere can be amazing at times. It is really a shame that all other gameplay elements are just pure garbage.
I would only recommend the game for people who like to be punished. It is extremely annoying and frustrating.
Have a nice day.

I’m going to say straight up I love this game. I don’t even know why you are reading this now just go and buy it. It has deep characters, interesting gameplay, and gameplay that makes my girlhood tremble. I don’t even understand why you’re even reading this at this point just go out and buy it’s a good game. Ten outta ten game of the year it deserves a cupcake. This game has literally consumed weeks of my life since the main release. I have at current time 124 hours of playtime in the game itself. If that’s any indicator of how I feel about this game. Although 4 of those hours were spent playing the early access version of this game which is far different from the end game. The end game is a polished masterpiece obviously crafted with love and care. This game goes to show that you can crowdfund a game and not have it come out like total♥♥♥♥♥♥(I’m looking at you Friday the 13th).
First I want to talk about the characters as they are a main centerpiece of this game. You can get a bunch of handmade losers with no back story but I don’t recommend it. I played with Lohse, The Red Prince and Sebille for my first play through of this game and each back story was rich and detailed and I really felt compelled to help them out and complete their goals and objectives. I’m not going to spoil it for anyone but I will definitely be playing again with all different characters because I genuinely enjoyed the rich character back story for your companions. They also did a good job fleshing out npc interactions making each encounter diverse I really felt like I was speaking with someone with a different life and personality every new encounter. ♥♥♥♥ing kudos to Larian Studios for creating something that destroyed hours of my life and consumed me for over a month.

Second I would like to gush over the brilliant combat system in this game. It’s ♥♥♥♥ing glorious. It can be hard at times but it’s balanced enough to keep you going even after you lose. It’s basically a top down strategy rpg combat systems and it is ♥♥♥♥ing brilliant. There is a complex list of different classes you can play as making the game diverse in the way of approaching combat. Of course you have your magic, tank and dps but you can also combine them to do multiple roles making characters absolute power houses. You also have to factor in environmental problems such as fire, poison, ice water and electricity all interact with each other in unique and interesting ways. Like you can call in a rain shower have another character light it on fire and fire lighting into the steam cloud to deal damage. It’s all very complex and real organic fun that makes me more erect than an NRA member in Somalia.
Third I want to talk about the story and it had its ups and downs. I feel like they may have extended it to be a bit too long. But take that with a grain of salt because I like completing everything when I play a game so that could also be why it took so much of my time.  But other than the above average length the actual content of the story is ♥♥♥♥ing enthralling. I couldn’t help but put myself in the shoes of my character and getting swept away by the depth of the lore.  Every new area was a new adventure to begin filled with mystery intrigue and danger. Don’t really want to spoil much just know that it is great if you are in it for the long haul. Do wish the ending was a little better though. I felt that no matter which choice I made had bad and good side to each. But that feels like a minor downside as every other aspect of the story is ♥♥♥♥ing fantastic.
My few minor complaints are that the game can be overly long. Towards the end I really was just looking for the light at the end of the tunnel. Not to say it wasn’t still enjoyable but after 100 hours of playing a game it does kinda of wear you down. Also even though the game can be challenging that does give you some frustration when you have to keep save scumming. Learn to save every chance you can because the autosave tries to do it every encounter but sometimes it helps to some saves lying around. But these are very minor details as far as the downsides.

I can't wait for future expansions to the northwest and south, and central regions!

As Overgrowth is finally nearing the full campaign launch and exiting beta, I have to say, I really love the work put into this game.
I've been tagging along with the game for a few years now, as many people have. At this point, it's worth noting that people aren't wrong - after years and years, we only finally got out of alpha. However, those years and years have been full of nothing but progress. Overgrowth is starting to take the form of a "true" game, instead of just getting to experiece a game being built, and it's as stunning now as it was years ago.
While gameplay definitely has a bit of a learning curve - I still refuse to do anything but punch enemies because I can't remember combat controls - it definitely functions as a complete, in-depth "fighting simulator", with enemies that are intuitive and force you to keep your focus. You can't just spam a combo and win your battles here, and it definitely adds to the immersion of the game. And, for those who come for just that aspect of the game and aren't interested in the campaigns much, the arena mode is more fleshed out and well-established than most like it.
With that said, combat is only a part of what the game is. I personally picked up Overgrowth when Mirror's Edge got me into parkour style games, and to this day, Overgrowth still satisfies those needs. The physics engine is still as impressive and beautiful as it was when the project was conceived and honestly, who wouldn't want to fling themselves across a map as a giant rabbit?
Of course, a nod to the content creators, as the Overgrowth team has never left them behind. Featuring an in-game mod menu for comprehensive modding and a level creator that every update gets more and more user friendly, Wolffire certainly has the interests of the community in mind.
And it shows. Honestly, I used to be in the same boat as a lot of others - the game was interesting and had a good concept, but was really lacking in true gameplay. But having gotten to see Overgrowth progress this far has been a hell of a journey, and I'm so, so excited to see the final product out of beta. It's clear that Wolffire has been working hard, that they listen to the community and incoporate feedback, and to be completely honest, I'm just really, really proud of seeing what an amazing game the Overgrowth team has produced.

Weird how this game gets negative reviews because of the skill ceiling. Last time I checked it's a good thing for a game to have a high skill ceiling. Chivalry has a big learning curve and skill gap, but that's what makes it a fun game. Dragging, feinting, rainbow overheads, stuff like that separates the game from other melee combat systems and makes it deep.
There are level 1-15 servers, with all noobs. Right after you pass level 15 you'll be thrown into the lion's den, and most people get mad and stop playing. Playing experience players feels daunting and ridiculous at first, but just have to play and learn techniques.  So if you're a casual player you might not enjoy this game.
People say this game is like "medieval call of duty", but they don't really translate. You'll probably like this game more if you like RPGs with hardcore melee combat, or fighting games.
All the reviews getting mad at "ballerinas" and "dragging" are just people who are bad at the game and get mad when experienced players demolish them with advanced techniques.

TLDR: Conan Exiles is an extremely fun game if you find the game mode that suits you and the right server.
Let me tell you my history with this game.
When it first came out on Steam I was like: “Cool, a new Conan game, always wanted to try one”. I was also intrigued by the fact that it was survival (never played a survival game ex: ARK), that it had RP-PvP servers (the two things I love about a MMO) and that it had the courage to exhibit nudity (indicating that they are going for a more mature audience).
Of course, I did not buy it right away, I waited for some reviews…and as it was to be expected, there were many negative ones. I shook my head and decided to wait some more time, for the game to be improved and check some more reviews as time passes.
I feel the need to mention that I work as a game tester and know very well what an early access / alpha game means. Bugs or features that do not work are not important to me, I know these things get fixed and are to be expected.
So, many months passed by and the game was still at the back of my mind every time I logged into steam. I even watched some let’s plays on youtube and the guys seemed to enjoy himself. Steam summer sales came so I said ♥♥♥♥ it, I really want to try it. So I bought it.
First thing I did was to enter a random RP-pvp server. The lag was pretty bad and after 1 hour of playing I was no one. I decided to change servers to see if I can find a more populated / better lag server. Well..that decision changed how I look at the game.
I joined a server that had RP rules (you can’t attack or raid other people without a RP reason) and had established clans around the map. After 1 hour I already made some RP friends and moved to a good area of the map where they helped me build a house.
My neighbors in the game are really nice people and we RP allot, we go on expeditions to kill things and gather materials.
The game honestly gives you the feeling that you are in a wild land, working with a community to survive.
All you need is to find the right server and the right game mode for you and it will give you a memorable experience. Yes, it has bugs and it can be laggy for a bit from time to time but these things will get fixed eventually. If you have patience you can see the gem lurking underneath.

The game only needs a few improvements to make it great.  I love the concept of building your own bot for combat (I remember playing flash games with the same concept a long time ago), but the F2P version is rather limiting. Yes, you can build a solid bot, but only having one to work with and only 9 part slots doesn't let you experiment very much.  You can easily get enough money to buy new parts since most are less than 10 coins (heavy sniper is 12) and you are guaranteed at least 3 coins per win regardess of performance (I've joined in as the game ended and got coins).  Additional coins are rewarded for doing well (extra coin at 5 kills, idk how many caps for an extra).
There are a balancing issue that need to be addressed (the most common loadout I've seen is a gatling primary and missile secondary), but the game does a decent job of trying to give everyone equal footing.  I've actually tried new weapons and gone back to the starter becasue it was better.  Anyways, I've read other reviews that say snipers rule the maps, which isn't true from what I've experiened.  I've rarely encountered a sniper, and you can easily take it out if it's close (extremely low fire rate), or hide behind something in the environment.  Since there aren't many wide open areas, snipers can easily be avoided.
The propulsion systems that don't contact the ground are very loose when it comes to control.  Since the turret controls are completely separated from the base, I often get disoriented and go somewhere I don't want to.  I wouldn't mind if they added something else to the screen to remind ou which way the base was facing.  On a separate note, the movement systems appear to take momentum into account.  Going up hills makes you an easy target if you don't get a running start, and levitating bases will drift if you turn without slowing down.
They did a very good job setting up the servers.  I haven't experienced the lag I occasionally see in other online games.
My main issue lies outside of the gameplay.  In the few days I've had the game, it's crashed to the point where I have to restart my system at least three times.  It blacked out my desktop when I alt+tabbed, so I couldn't force it to close with the task manager.
If they manage to fix that, this could be one of my favorite games.

Definitely unique within the current roster of MOBA games. The character cast is smaller than League of Legends or DotA 2, but there's just enough of them to fulfill most roles you'd come to expect — and a few you wouldn't — with more added regularly. Graphics are nice, but can run on lower-end systems fairly well. Music tends to be pretty jammin', too. If you have a poor Internet connection, you might encounter a lot of lag and random disconnections, the former of which can really annoy people since it gives some characters an undue advantage (looking at you, Coco), and a lot of people exploit that intentionally. Still, the community is leagues above most other MOBAs, with people that will actually try to help new players as opposed to bash them as useless scum on the sea floor deserving of prompt immolation, which is a refreshing change of pace. On top of all that, you don't have to pay to unlock characters, as they come the more you play — only extra skins for those characters cost anything, and there's a couple you can get for free, even.
All in all, definitely a fantastic game to pick up. Incredibly fun, gives a taste unlike other MOBAs and a lot of games in general, and is continuing to grow.

As mentioned before, there's issues that should have been obvious to address in alpha. For example the game seems unable to remember your resolution settings properly. Every time i tab out of the game, it went into window mode, and i had to go back into settings to reset the resolution. Additionally, the game seems to require way more resources to run than necessary. It's visually appealing, but not as graphic intense as most games that run comfortably on older macines. Finally, the actual resolution of the game doesn't match the resolution denomination in the settings. When i put 1080X768, the game seemed like a stretched out 400X300. It litterally looks like a game on the Nintendo 64 console.
There's also a lot of gameplay issues. Often a player will spawn as invisible, or be competely indestructible, and overall, the experience isn't that much different from other free to play games that can be found on the web.
Had the product been in alpha or early beta when i tested this, my review would have been different, but it seems that the game is nearing the end of beta at the time this review was written, and the above mentioned problems are still evident.

*edit: I spent 2 more hours on this game to get into the top 10% of the leaderboard (at the time) and to make another video because I was unfair in the one I linked here.  My opinion is unchanged.
Frankly, there isn't anywhere close to 5 dollars worth of content in this game.  You get one relatively small arena with no physical obstacles, no differentiation in how the game begins, with one gun that supposedly upgrades as you proceed (though admittedly I'm not good enough to get that far).  You know what else you can get for 5 dollars?  The Binding of Isaac.
There is a replay feature that you can find from the leaderboards to see how the best of the best get through it, which is actually pretty cool.  That's a feature I'd love to see in more games in some capacity.
I can respect what this game wants to do with its movement and its graphical style and its engine and I think all that is really cool, but it simply needs more.  One arena with one gun with one set of waves simply is not enough.  What really confuses me is how this game currently has over 90 positive reviews singing its praises and only 7 negative reviews that are constantly being flagged as "unhelpful" for some reason.  It almost seems a little bit sketchy, as I've seen better games get♥♥♥♥♥♥on for less.

At first I was hesitant at getting this. It looks great, and like a lot of fun, but maybe not worth the price. I thought maybe I'd pick up the game on a sale or something.
But I'm very glad I got it.
The story is very rich and there's so many ways to play. I'm excited for my second and third play throughs.
You can steal from anybody, kill anyone, befriend NPCs, talk to your followers if you choose to have them, and each story is different from character creation. Each race is treated differently, you have different dialogue options if you're an Outlaw, or Scholar, or even if you play a smart Wizard, you can persuade people with your smarts, or intimidate people with your strength.
The combat is very fun, and comboing spells and attacks is awesome.
Classes aren't really set in stone either. If you're a Fighter but decide you want to shock people, or grow some wings, you can very much do so.
And the GM mode is amazing.
As a Game Master for D&D games, I've always wanted a game to play it in, to immerse the players, and let them explore with out having to explain every small detail. And this game does it very well. You can create custom items, NPCs (even down to what hat they wear), allies, and customize the pre set maps the game gives you. I would honestly buy a DLC that includes more maps. But there are plently right now, I'm just afraid that through multiple play throughs we'll all think "Oh, this map again."
This game is a masterpiece, but it's not perfect.
The combat is very hard, even on the easiest difficulty it sometimes feels like I need to kill a couple NPCs who don't deserve it so I can level up and continue the story. And sometimes this makes the game feel linear. I don't know if I'm missing something, or I chose bad classes for my party, but either way that's a big down side for me.
That being said, at the time of posting this review I'm 71 hours in, and I havent even completed my first play through, which is a good thing. I'm taking my time, exploring the world, talking to every NPC and living the world.
UPDATE (very minor spoilers):
I finished the game, and I have to say while the ending was good, it was very buggy. I was unable to use res scrolls, enemies would teleport everywhere, and some other minor things.
Arx also felt very bland for what it could have been. Driftwood and all of Reaper's Coast felt huge, and there was so much story there, but Arx... You were there for one thing, and that was to beat the game. I tried to find more to do there, I tried to find side quests, just anything, but there was nothing. Maybe I missed stuff, maybe I didn't. Either way I feel the game no longer deserves my original score of 8.5/10.

Woodle Tree Adventures is overall a very fun, unique, cute, addictive, and challenging game. It is similar to Super Mario Galaxy in the way that you must travel to different floating worlds and parkour your way through them.
But like any game, it has its flaws.
Firstly, the camera angles. Sometimes, the camera will be stuck at a very uncomfortable angle, making it nigh impossible to see where you are going, resulting in falling into the same pit 50 times.
Another thing it lacks is consistent checkpoints. Where you die effects where you will respawn, but you actually have to die to see where that place will be. Its different in each place, and doesn't make sense.  For example, on the beehive level, if you died about a third of the way through the level, you respawned just barely before there. But if you died near the end of the level, you had to start all the way over. It was also stuck on a very annoying camera angle the whole time, which made it rather difficult and infuriating.
Aside from that, I rather enjoy the cute graphics, music, unique story, and fun gameplay. I do recommend it to those who enjoy playing casual indie games from time to time to quench boredom.

Weird how this game gets negative reviews because of the skill ceiling. Last time I checked it's a good thing for a game to have a high skill ceiling. Chivalry has a big learning curve and skill gap, but that's what makes it a fun game. Dragging, feinting, rainbow overheads, stuff like that separates the game from other melee combat systems and makes it deep.
There are level 1-15 servers, with all noobs. Right after you pass level 15 you'll be thrown into the lion's den, and most people get mad and stop playing. Playing experience players feels daunting and ridiculous at first, but just have to play and learn techniques.  So if you're a casual player you might not enjoy this game.
People say this game is like "medieval call of duty", but they don't really translate. You'll probably like this game more if you like RPGs with hardcore melee combat, or fighting games.
All the reviews getting mad at "ballerinas" and "dragging" are just people who are bad at the game and get mad when experienced players demolish them with advanced techniques.

Don't listen to the negative reviews and try it out for yourself, after all it is free.
I have put quite a few hours into this game since releasing on Steam and I am enjoying it, although I am only halfway through the campaign. There is quite a high cost if you want to pay to play but it is easily playable without spending any money, I have only paid for VIP but without people spending money the game would shut down.
Pros
- Enjoyable enough to sink some time into
- Five different types of modes, each with their own energy system.
- Definately don't have to pay to play, you will sometimes bump into someone with really strong cards but not often
- Matches are quick, maybe a minute each
- As of writing there are thirty levels of campaign each with there own star system to earn the cards.
- Earn lots of money in game, not premium currency, to buy card packs. Hint, save up and buy max cards as I got a few epics this way.
Cons
- You don't get a lot of energy, even with VIP, so you may have to return a few times per day to maximise your levelling, you can add a larger maximum cap for real money.
- Timers are ridiculous, over an hour to get one piece of energy for the arena and researching the later combos can take 48 hours, so I have heard, not got there myself yet with my longest research taking 24 hours. You can pay real money for the machine that speeds up research.
- No real PVP. You are literally playing against a bot that chooses the cards in the players deck. Real PVP needs adding, if you are looking for a Hearthstone or Elder Scrolls Legends clone this is not it.
- It is a chore to sell all common cards, you have to remove them manually from each deck which has no option, that I can see, to remove all the cards from a deck.
Please do not listen to the reviews, try it and see if you like it yourself. I almost never downloaded it after reading the reviews first but I am happy I did. I really hope they keep adding to the game.

A basic trading/simple quest game that falls a little flat in the end.
There are two keys to the game that you are required to do in order to finish but there is no way to really know that until you get to the end making the game unfinishable in that play through. Unfortunately, the game isn't enjoyable enough or deep enough to justify a 2nd play though. I really can't say more without spoilers which I will add below for those who do wish to buy the game and beat it on the first play through.
********* Quick Walkthrough *************
You need a rank 9ish mercenary and merchant to complete the final quests. There is limited good exp from quests in the game so if you don't hire one of each fairly early and level them up to 9ish by the end, it will be pretty much impossible to do so. The highest level merchant you can hire is rank 7 which is no where high enough to complete the final quest. The only way to get any exp once you reach the final quests is extremely random encounters that you can fight to receive a measly 50 exp per encounter making it completely unfeasible to level any characters late game. This is a game breaking issue at that point making the game unfinishable.
The other classes outside of mercenary and merchant do not really matter all that much although a sage can be somewhat helpful early on before you mercenary gets OP.

Oh boy reviewing MMOs, here we go.
Pros:
- This MMO is really, REALLY fun. I don't know what it is but the gameplay just clicks with me.
- Class diversity is alright.
- Playing with friends is fun.
- Distinct MMO feel but more actiony than most MMOs where you stand in a spot and hit buttons; movement and repositioning are very important aspects of the game.
- Grind is MUCH less grindy than most MMOs - quests give a huge chunk of EXP so hitting level cap is fairly easy.
- Game rewards skill to a certain degree. I think you can solo all the content in the game if you're good enough. As a solo player this appeals to me.
- Lovely aesthetics/visuals.
- Runs pretty smooth on my GTX660 (60FPS for the most part except during massive fights/explosions)
Cons:
- Pay2Win. No way around it, this game is 100% Nexon, which means 100% P2W. Cash items give stats, helpers give stats/autoloot, you can get gambling boxes that can randomly drop stat-giving items, etc. If you don't think this game is P2W you're a moron.
- Marketplace is desaturated at lower levels. When I played this game around its release date you could easily find gear for your class/level on the marketplace for reasonable prices, and sell the extra gear you found that you didn't need for around the same amount, but now that the heavy users are all capped out the marketplace is super end-game heavy and super expensive.
- Pay2Win. I had to list this twice, this really pisses me off. The game could've been 20000x better without the P2W aspects.
- Daily softcaps on dungeons. You get 700 PWR per day and 500 bonus per week, and dungeons cost PWR (I think 12-30 or something). PWR gives you bonus EXP while in dungeons, which means that if you spend your 1200 PWR in a day you don't get bonus EXP and you get gimped. I know at some point before this used to be a hard cap (ie you couldn't enter dungeons at ALL if you had 0 PWR) but I think you can dungeon without PWR now (not 100% sure). This is a minor gripe as it only really affects people playing 6+ hours a day (which I sometimes do).
Overall:
I do recommend the game if you like the gameplay and visual styles. There's PvP and PvE in the game (both very prominent end-game) and, being quest-based grind, it doesn't feel as grindy as some other MMORPGs. Pay2Win sucks but Nexon is going to be Nexon so unless someone else takes over DN and removes the P2W aspects it's probably just going to get worse (look at Maplestory).

There are not as many jRPGs for PCs as I would like to see these days  and this one begins with a great  intro (If one is not allergic to anime. But if so, this game should be avoided at all costs), and features a cozy, classic jRPG art style of 3D backgrounds with pre-rendered actors.  The battle system is also quick and enjoyable, if  a bit simple.
That said, there are some things not that great concerning this game. First of all, it’s not particularly long for a role-play. Beating the game should take no more than 15 hours (and it is entirely possible to complete the storyline in about 5) which is not all that impressive concerning the fact that some other jRPGs have mini-games that are more time consuming.
After completing the campaign, you can try the time attack or replay the story on another difficulty setting. There is no incentive to do so, since perhaps the Oath’s weakest point is its plot. The story told is extremely generic and predictable. Furthermore, the 30-some cast of characters is largely uninteresting. Finally, the extremely pompous  dialogue (and I do say that as a fan of jRPG narration) lines do not help at all.
There aren’t  that many items to be collected either –  6 sets of equipment (sword, shield and armor each – all with 3 levels of upgrades ), 3 (also upgradeable 3 times )spells,  24 other items (usable, plot tokens or granting a particular ability). And , which is quite surprising in this genre – no party can be formed at any point of the game – the protagonist is forever alone (in battle) .
What saves the day and, in the end, redeems this otherwise average game, are some of the most brilliant boss- battles I have ever seen in a jRPG game: quick, demanding and almost perfectly balanced to avoid the excessive grind (at least on the medium difficulty setting).
Concluding, this is not a greatly memorable title and in the end I feel that it abused my longing for a classic jRPG experience, which  kept me in front of the computer until the end. 6 out of 10, and I recommend it solely due to the awesomeness of  boss battles.

Absolutely having a BLAST in Conan Exiles!  I was a bit wary in purchasing this game due to the mixed reviews, but (for me) I love the world of Hyboria and decided to take the plunge and buy it.  I'm glad I did.  Most negative reviews were due to hackers, but I play on those servers that run BattleEye (not sure if that makes much of a difference) and never saw anything like that.  I was particular in which servers I chose, though, opting for a couple of the custom servers that have active admins.
Anyway, after I bought the game for myself I told my cousin about it and he bought it.  I then purchased a copy for a friend of mine.  Afterwards, I set up a local dedicated server for us (and potential friends/family) to play on.  It took some work, but finally got it up and running.
The server customization is really nice.  I do NOT like to cheat, but I do like to use a pick, axe, or sword that doesn't break every 4 people it hits, so being able to decrease the damage durability modifier was nice to have.  I also didn't like how fast the nighttime passed, so I lowered the speed multiplier of night and day.  I also didn't enjoy having my food spoil WHILE I ate it (lol), so I lowered the time it takes for food to spoil to the lowest setting where it would still spoil, but not crazy-fast.  These are just some of the settings you can tweak to better customize YOUR experience.  I have to say it's working out rather nicely.
Additional Pros:
--Server stability:  Very nice.  It's hard to believe that the game is early access with how well it runs.  I have never experienced a crash to desktop while playing in the game.  It runs smoothly, with very little to no lag spikes during gameplay.  Grant it, I only have a small number of friends and family playing, but it runs very smooth.
--Graphics:  Beautiful game.  From the landscape to the animals, from the sky to the water (and waterfalls) this game is just gorgeous.  I'm able to have draw distance up to Ultra, and it's just a beautiful work of art.  The sandstorms are just a wonder to behold.
--Sound:  Sound is really well-done. From the different movement/running sound when wearing No/Light/Medium armor(s) is pretty cool.  It actually FEELS like you're wearing heavier armor while playing.  Funcom did a really good job here, in my opinion.  Environment sounds are really good as well.  The difference in nighttime/daytime creature sounds is really enjoyable.
--Music:  Movie and MMO soundtrack, the Conan Universe music in this game is phenomenal.  It truly makes me want to go re-watch the movies.
--Gameplay:  I've touched on this already, but one thing I failed to mention is just how awesome the construction system is.  I don't have the time to go into the details, but it's one of the best I've ever seen.  You can build just about anyTHING you want and put it just about anyWHERE you want.  It's a VERY impressive system that I recommend to anyone that enjoys building (minecraft, sims, etc...)
Cons:  To be honest, there are very few cons to mention, but they do exist:
--Bugs:  It's early access.  There are bugs.  We all know this.  Altar of Set preventing nearby building, object cannot be placed (relog sometimes remedies), etc...
--Creature Animations:  They're pretty rough at times.  Hyenas that "slide" toward you as they remain in the sitting/lounging pose is funny, but it's immersive-breaking.  For the most part, the animals do what they're supposed to, but there are quite a few times when I've encountered random silliness.  I've come to accept it, though.  It's Early Access, remember? :)
--Map System:  Not very good.  However, the upcoming patch is bringing a new, colorful map that remedies most, if not all, the problems I have with the current system.  This includes being able to pin notes to the map (this is a HUGE issue and really needed).  Also, the patch will include exploration notifications that give xp when discovering "important" areas.  The next patch is really anticipated.
--Solo/CO-OP Mode:  There are TWO things that really bothered me in this mode:  1)  Tethering.  As the host, anyone that you invite to your game is "tethered" to you, preventing you to ever leave each other's side and explore/harvest/fight on your own.  This was the MAIN reason why I put together my own dedicated server.  2)  CO-OP Animation:  I don't know why, but when I was host the client(s) that joined me had characters that looked jerky and very unsmooth animations.  It's not like they were lagging (appearing in one place then appearing somewhere else).  Instead the actual movement and animations of my friends' characters just looked as if they were operating at about 2/3 the speed of everything else. It was very weird and VERY noticeable.  When we play on a dedicated server, this problem vanished.
No Quests/Friendly NPC's/Friendly Towns:
It plays like Skyrim but it's far different from Skyrim.  Unless you play on a server with other people, it's going to be very lonely.  Even with a couple of friends, it can be lonely as everyone you meet is potentially an enemy or a (future) thrall.  Maybe down the road there will be NPCs, but don't count on it.  This is a game where the players ARE the community and that's just fine with me (well, for the most part...depends on the players, lol).  Just be aware that this is NOT a game where you speak with an NPC, get a Quest, then go do it and turn it in.
FINAL THOUGHTS:
Conan Exiles is a great game.  I've seen launched titles perform worse and offer little more in content that what Funcom has given us (as of 7/2/2017).  With a new, free expansion coming in August, and a new engine upgrade and new features in the near-future patch, Conan Exiles has a LOT to offer.  Keep in mind it's still EARLY ACCESS and you'll see that Funcom has done a tremendous job on a title that hasn't even launched.
I'm having a blast and hope you do as well.

Sorath
is a first-person endless shooter developed and published by Sorath.
The custom made engine works fludly and the game does look really good, with a strong Doom vibe from all the monsters you fight. I would like to see something more in the area in which you fight, like small obstacles or walls, because like this it tends to get repetitive.
Your goal is to survive an endless wave of monsters for as long as you can. Your only weapon is an unlimited amount of daggers that you shoot from your hand. The longer you play, more monsters start appearing, and you unlock some bonuses for your attack. You can also bunnyhop to gain more speed.
This is literally the entire game. It's simple, straight-forward and hard to master. It does get very repetitive after a while, and it works better in short game sessions.
The game is tough as nails: you die with one hit by either getting hit by enemies, running into them, or falling off the map. Only masochists and hardcore Quake fans will really enjoy playing this game.
The sound design is pretty solid, however it does lack a lot in music and you will easily get annoyed by the constant throwing of daggers and monster noises after a bunch of minutes.
You also want to play another time, just to get a higher score. But you probably won't. It gets very frustrating, but if you like to get better scores every time you will most definitely spend hours and hours mastering this game.
Overall, fans of endless shooters will have a blast playing this game, and for its cheap price I do recommend it. Remember that it is tough as nails and kind of repetitive in the long run.

Ys The Oath in Felghana is a remake of Ys III in the Ys series. It had a massive overhaul from the original that includes gameplay, style, graphics, and music. It's action RPG goodness to say the least. I know veteran fans will blast me, but think of Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past on crack with a lot of enemies, 80's rock and power metal, tough bosses, and leveling, but without the puzzles, exploration and Zelda.
If you want to jump in to the series, I recommend you play it on Easy first. Normal isn't that hard but the bosses will punish you for mistakes. The bosses themselves don't look bad and they have set patterns but dodging is harder than it looks and if you can't keep up BOOM! That's a tenth or more of your health gone.
There's also a bit of level scaling to the table. Say a boss is level 15, and you're level 12. You are going to get mopped on the floor. It's possible but it's really hard. Climb up to level 15 and you should be okay. Level up to 16. It's almost a joke! For the most part.
Lastly, you don't have to play the past series to understand the story because each entry in the series is a new adventure. Ys I and II are the execptions because they're sequels to each other.
